newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER-BENARBIA FIRES MONACO INTO SEMIFINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BENARBIA FIRES MONACO INTO SEMIFINALS.

text.p: Midfielder Ali Benarbia scored two second half goals as Monaco crushed Newcastle United 3-0 in the home leg of their UEFA Cup quarter-final on Tuesday to reach the semifinals 4-0 on aggregate.

The French league leaders went in front four minutes before halftime when midfielder Sylvain Legwinski robbed the ball from Peter Beardsley 30 metres out, took three steps and blasted it from the edge of the box past diving goalkeeper Shaka Hislop and just inside his left post.
Seven minutes into the second half the busy Benarbia, heir to Belgian Enzo Scifo as Monaco's playmaker, was in the box to volley home a cross from the right by defender Patrick Blondeau.

Benarbia put the tie totally beyond Newcastle's reach in the 67th minute when he curled a brilliant free kick from the left inside the near post after Robert Lee had fouled Brazilian striker Anderson.
Monaco, only the third French side to eliminate an English team in European competition, are now just one round from their second European final after playing in the 1993 Cup Winners' Cup final.

They had the clearer chances before they scored, but Newcastle also threatened Fabien Barthez's goal and the France keeper showed he had learnt typically British attributes by coming out well to cut out dangerous crosses.
Newcastle manager Kenny Dalglish said: "At 0-0 I think they were getting a bit nervous. The (first) goal gave them a lift.
"It could have been different if it had stayed 0-0 at halftime."

Right back Steve Watson was given a torrid time by teenager Thierry Henry, whose pace put him through several times on the left flank in the first half. Henry also brought Hislop to a diving save by the near post.
Watson cleared for a corner as Anderson looked set to head home a cross from the right by Benarbia early in the game.
Central defender Philippe Albert also headed clear a chip by Benarbia in the first half after Darren Peacock denied Benarbia in Monaco's first penetrating attack.
Newcastle's three-pronged attack of Frenchman David Ginola, Beardsley and Colombian striker Tino Asprilla had their efforts snuffed out by a well-drilled Monaco defence.

With the score 2-0, Watson put across a dangerous low ball from the right that defender Martin Djetou and Barthez combined to clear from the lurking Asprilla, who was not given room to reproduce his recent scintillating English premier league form.
The introduction of winger Keith Gillespie for Beardsley midway through the second half made no difference.
"I don't think the players could have given any more in terms of commitment. They're a very good French side," Dalglish said.
"They make it very difficult to play, they're very organised and they've got pace up front.
"It'll be a good side that beats them," he added when asked if he saw Monaco winning the trophy.
Monaco coach Jean Tigana said: "I don't care who we get next. I think only about preparing my team to win."
